extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, reviewers and editors at Royal Society journals and the broader scholarly publishing community
extracted.subtask_description: Principles, practices and observed impacts of adopting open/transparent peer review (including identity-disclosure options, reviewer recognition, and related open-data policies) in journal publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review: publish reports alongside articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish peer review reports alongside articles (transparent peer review) so readers can see the review history and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society Open Science launched with this model and it is 'baked into that journal’s identity'; several journals have since adopted similar approaches. Transparency is implemented by making reports available alongside the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer option to reveal identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Give reviewers the option to reveal their identity when peer review reports are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher 'leave[s] it up to the reviewer to decide if they want their identity revealed' and recognises there are good reasons (beyond bias concerns) for a reviewer to choose anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise peer review reports as citable scientific outputs (DOIs/ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign digital object identifiers (DOIs) to peer review reports and enable their recognition as scholarly outputs that reviewers can include in ORCID records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working with Web of Science Reviewer Recognition allows peer review reports to be assigned DOIs, 'making it easier for reviewers [to] include their peer review work in their ORCID records' and supporting professional recognition of review activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow publisher amendment of author identity where safety requires
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend published author identities when authors express concerns about differences between their published and 'real' identities and when separation is important for safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher notes they have, on occasion, amended author identities to protect authors' safety and to respect the need for separation between public and real identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active efforts to encourage inclusive and diverse engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively encourage engagement from a more inclusive and diverse demographic (geographical and gender diversity) among authors, editors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed changes in stakeholder make-up are 'partly a result of our active efforts to encourage the engagement of a more inclusive and diverse demography in our journals' — publishers should combine policy with outreach to increase participation from under-represented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness increases visibility and engagement of historically under-represented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency in peer review increases visibility of under-represented groups, which in turn encourages more engagement from those groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As 'the identities of our stakeholders becomes clearer to our readers', this visibility may encourage readers to write, review or edit for journals, helping bring in non-Western and more gender-representative contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review promotes better reviewing practices and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing reviews helps improve reviewing quality because reading examples of good and poor reviews aids learning, especially for early-career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog states that 'reading what makes a good or less-than-good review helps particularly early-career scientists to write better reviews themselves' and promotes reviewers' identities as constructive, collaborative scientists. Use of published reviews as teaching examples is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review and open data increase reader confidence to raise queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater openness in peer review combined with open data policies makes readers more confident to raise queries arising from published reviews or datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This increased confidence 'reinforces the identities of the journals as being bastions of scientific rigour' and helps journals identify and correct errors in the scientific record by encouraging post-publication scrutiny and queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness contributes to journal identity as rigorous and accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting openness in peer review and data policies helps shape the journal's identity as committed to scientific rigour and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog positions openness as reinforcing journal identity: not only ensuring high-quality review but also 'recognising where we err and doing our best to correct the scientific record.' Openness is framed as part of the journal's brand and mission.
